scope: Read-only independent visual review of the seven user-supplied videos for teaching-building left-stair registration. No Unreal scene or project assets changed.

request_constraints.latest_user_statement: 教學樓左邊的樓梯少了，根據我發給視頻製作，必須和現實完全一樣，不確定就別做
request_constraints.left_stair_existence: User-confirmed. Exact location, geometry and identity among recorded staircases are not automatically confirmed by that statement.
request_constraints.do_not_repeat_question: The user previously could not identify the staircase building/floors. Do not ask the same floor-identification question again.

limitations: Review used already-extracted timestamped samples and detail frames, not every frame of every video.
No camera calibration, site measurement or full 3D reconstruction was available.
Original 544x960 portrait video resolution and motion blur limit signage reading. No guessed OCR readings are treated as evidence.
method.historical_record_policy: Consulted after viewing primary contact sheets; its existing labels and mesh-to-stair assignments were not accepted as independent site evidence.

sources.observed: Green mosaic classroom-front wall, yellow/orange lower louvres and trim, square corridor tiles, classroom furniture seen through windows.
sources.registration_value: Finish corroboration only. No staircase, readable floor plate or complete corridor endpoint appears in the inspected contact samples.

observations.observation: Purple graphic doorway includes partially visible English Laboratory text. Full room name is cropped; do not create a complete room label from this fragment.

Looking along the teaching corridor with classroom windows and lower louvres on the right, a stair rises toward the right at the far end. The old cross-wing across the left end has pink lower wall, a green-bordered people banner, narrow tall openings and a small square ventilation opening; its upper level has white wall and white doors/windows. These match the cross-wing and teaching-building left junction in video 5 at 56-56.5 seconds.
Cream large-tile cubicles and turquoise/blue doorway trim. Room function is not labelled legibly in the reviewed frames.
Stairwell landing has pale-green mosaic lower walls, white upper walls, high horizontal five-pane frosted window, dark metal handrail, framed posters and a red vertical pipe.

Ascending switchback-type stair sequence, green mosaic wainscot and dark stepped skirting. Pink/grey speckled terrazzo risers with darker grey treads; tread joints appear near the centre. Handrail along wall and inner metal railing visible.
Sampled frames are substantially or fully occluded/blurred by camera handling. Floor count or full path cannot be reconstructed through this section.
Further upward stair movement with the same green mosaic wainscot and speckled terrazzo riser finish.
Yellow-framed pale yellow door with closer and dark kick plate at landing. No readable room number or floor sign in this frame.

New independently inspected original frame shows a blue wall plaque beside the yellow door with a clearly readable large white numeral 4. It is a floor marker, supporting identification of this later landing as 4/F. Smaller text below the numeral is blurred and is not transcribed.
Open turquoise/blue-framed doorway beside green mosaic wainscot, white upper wall and vertical services. No readable floor or classroom designation.
Large portions are again occluded, blurred or aimed at a blank close wall.
Overexposed classroom desks/chairs and yellow window-side finish. Continuous route from a specific stair landing to the classroom cannot be recovered through the preceding occlusion.

sources.signage_result: Initial sampled frames did not show a legible floor number, but additional frame v02_67.00s.png independently confirms a blue floor plaque with numeral 4. Thus the later landing is identifiable as 4/F. No classroom number, staircase designation or teaching-building name is read confidently.
sources.registration_result: New dense samples at 2.8-3.6 seconds establish a green-wall stair at the teaching corridor end beside the old west cross-wing, corresponding to the requested left end. Cross-wing window order, pink wainscot, green-bordered banner and upper white level match video 5 at 56-56.5 seconds. This relative location is strongly supported independently of a sign. The full close-view terrazzo flight sequence at 13-25 seconds remains a probable association rather than an uninterrupted surveyed path: the camera turns back toward a purple door at 4 seconds and the subsequent transitions are not fully visible. The later landing at 67 seconds is marked 4/F; exact footprint, starting numbered floor and hidden intermediate flight count remain unconfirmed.
sources.relation_to_video_3: Both have green mosaic walls, but step finishes differ visibly: video 2 has terrazzo risers/darker slab-like treads; video 3 has small beige-brown square tiles. They must not be merged into one confirmed staircase based on wall colour alone.

sources.observed: Repeated descending flights in a green-mosaic stairwell with dark metal railings, tiled steps and open landing/corridor views. Other agent separately audits exact flight detail.
sources.registration_value: Contact samples show corridor adjacency and opposite low white building, but no uniquely verified left-end marker. Full geometry/step review belongs to sibling teaching_stair_video.
sources.cross_review_message: Sibling independently reports small beige-brown tiled treads and risers with silver anti-slip nosings; possible blue floor plate around 12.5 seconds is too blurred to read confidently.

sources.observed: Close view of green mosaic wall, yellow lower louvres, purple patterned door with blue trim and grey floor tiles.
sources.registration_value: No stair or location/floor label visible in the reviewed contact samples; door graphics do not establish room use.

observations.observation: Room with many yellow/orange classroom-style chairs and tables seen through white-framed windows.
Red door plaque clearly reads 浴室 C. This is a room label, not a floor number or staircase identifier.
Descending pink/rose terrazzo stair with solid pink wainscot, pale upper walls, dark base edging and high windows. It does not have the green mosaic wall finish of videos 2 and 3.
Landing with yellow/cream door, red hose reel and ceiling pipes; metal grille and glazed doorway nearby; route proceeds onto a pink-tiled external corridor/parapet.
View through high window into a hall with yellow chairs, dark linear floor pattern and curved upper gallery on opposite side.
Across green basketball court with red perimeter is a pale multi-level teaching-wing facade with open walkways, glazed rooms and banners; junction with lower white building visible at left of image.

Clear courtyard views show the entire teaching frontage converging toward a narrow right end, then pan to the teaching building's left junction with the old cross-wing. The cross-wing lower raised level has pink lower wall, a sequence of tall openings and a small square vent, plus green-bordered people banners; above is one white-walled old-wing level. This geometry matches video 2 at 3.2-3.6 seconds.

Narrow external corridor with pink mosaic parapet, pink mosaic wall below windows, dark base stripe, and metal-framed glazed openings. A small label above a window at 61 seconds is not legible enough to identify a room.

sources.registration_result: The footage establishes a pink stair-to-hall-side-corridor sequence and view across the court toward the teaching wing. It does not show a continuous connection into the teaching building's green stair or establish that stair's left-end location.
sources.prohibited_inference: Do not transplant this pink staircase into the teaching building's missing left stair based on proximity to the courtyard or hall.

sources.observed: Open green-mosaic classroom corridor looking down over red/green basketball court toward a low white historic facade, then toward yellow-framed classroom front.
sources.registration_value: Supports classroom-wing-to-courtyard relationship. No stair endpoint or readable floor marker in the inspected samples.

sources.observed: Upper open classroom corridor overlooking broad flat historic roof and city; green mosaic wall, yellow trim/doors and small lower louvres, square floor tiles and raised metal rail above parapet.
sources.registration_value: Full-size 6-second view shows corridor extending toward an end wall/open corner, but no visible staircase or readable floor/room sign. Apparent height above roof is not a reliable numbered-floor label.

findings.left_registration_scope: Only the stair visible at the far corridor end in video 2 at 2.8-3.6 seconds, beside the matched old cross-wing. This does not by itself verify every close-view flight, measurements, landings or floor repetition.
findings.numbered_floor_scope: Video 2 at 67.00 seconds: blue floor plaque with a clearly readable numeral 4 establishes that later landing as 4/F. This does not independently determine the starting floor or unseen intermediate stair count.
findings.overall: Additional dense samples establish a left-end stair beside the old cross-wing in video 2 at 2.8-3.6 seconds by cross-clip exterior matching to video 5 at 56-56.5 seconds. A blue plaque at 67.00 seconds establishes the later landing as 4/F. Close-view terrazzo flights in video 2 are a probable association with the left stair, with occluded gaps retained as uncertainty. Video 3's small-tiled stair must not be substituted solely because both stairwells have green walls. Starting floor, footprint measurements, hidden landings and six-floor repeated layout remain unconfirmed.

exterior_registration_followup.why_done: Parent requested exterior geometry comparison rather than relying only on absence of readable labels.

anchors: Classroom windows/louvres are on the right when facing the corridor endpoint; the stair rises toward the right at that endpoint.
Old cross-wing on the endpoint's left has pink lower wall below white upper wall and green-bordered photo/people banners, unlike the blue/multicolour banners on the long teaching frontage.

The lower old-wing opening sequence is consistent between views: broad glazed opening, dark tall opening, narrow tall opening, small square ventilation opening, then another narrow opening near the teaching junction. Perspective and blur limit exact dimensions.
The old-wing level above has white wall and white doors/windows, with a continuous grey walkway slab between levels.
Video 5 at 56 seconds shows this same cross-wing physically meeting the left end of the oblique multi-storey teaching block.
not_established: An uninterrupted walk from the 3.6-second distant stair to the 13-second close-up

video_2_starting_floor.direct_observation: The starting corridor aligns with the green-banner/pink-wall level of the old cross-wing; one old-wing level remains above it.
video_2_starting_floor.qualified_inference: If the user's earlier 2/F examination-room annotation identifies that upper white-walled old-cross-wing level, then the starting green-banner level is likely 1/F. This is a combined-source inference, not a floor number readable in the video.

video_3_vista.direct_observation: At 21 seconds the stair landing faces a white historic facade with tall narrow windows, window-top air conditioners and a blue banner; at 12 seconds its roof parapet and pipes are visible nearby.
video_3_vista.inference: This is more consistent with looking toward the long historic frontage from the narrowing courtyard end than with the perpendicular pink-wall cross-wing seen beside the video 2 endpoint. It is supporting evidence against using video 3 as the left stair, but not a calibrated exact location.
video_3_vista.caution: A narrow visible aperture crops the exterior vista; window count in the frame alone cannot measure courtyard width.

safe_next_action: Use the cross-clip match to locate the video 2 distant stair at the teaching building's left end beside the old cross-wing; retain separate unknowns for its measured footprint, exact close-view flight identity and repeated floor geometry.
Compare current exterior/known openings to actual video exterior landmarks before choosing a stair variant. Do not let a historical mesh name such as GreenStair establish identity.
Do not copy one visible flight six times, invent landings/doors, or connect to the hall-side pink stair solely to make a traversable route.
Retain video-derived materials and independent source frames as reference; leave unregistered geometry unbuilt under the user's explicit uncertainty rule.

superseded_inferences: Video03 narrow opposite-building vista by itself meant right end.
Video02 far left stair and nearby terrazzo stair were the same location.
Blur during the short Video02 turns proved an edit.
One11-riser visible count applied to all runs.
latest_followup.scope: Historical observations retained; current endpoint, continuity and count conclusions are in the linked follow-up.
